# Index of Major Examples

Use this index to revisit the cases, demonstrations, and worked examples most likely to appear in class discussion and application questions. **Evidence role** states what the example can do. A demonstration or illustration can reveal a possibility; it is not by itself evidence of prevalence, effect size, causality, or generality.

## Recurring case map

These cases return because each appearance should add a new analytical layer rather than restart the example.

| Recurring case | Introduced | What later chapters add |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Hiring and selection** | Chapter 1 maps the hidden process and Chapter 2 constructs alternatives, forecasts, values, and a reviewable recommendation. | Attention changes what becomes evidence; intuitive judgment and comparison change candidate impressions; base rates improve prediction; culture changes the meaning of “fit”; decision hygiene redesigns elicitation, aggregation, documentation, and review. |
| **Supplier capacity and project risk** | Decisions from experience shows how a local sample can hide rare failure. | Strategic interdependence adds reciprocal response; negotiation reveals interests and priority differences; contingent agreements define evidence, responsibility, review, and exit. |
| **Defensive workplace conversation** | Chapter 39 maps the cue, defensive response, immediate relief, and recovery path. | Communication tests interpretations; connection and repair address impact and trust; decision hygiene protects dissent and learning. |
| **Employment or service agreement** | Chapter 2 treats acceptance as one option within a wider feasible set. | Negotiation adds BATNA, reservation value, opening and movement, value-creating packages, contingent terms, implementation, and review. |
| **Retirement or subscription path** | Time and mental accounting explain why an endorsed future can lose influence at the moment of action. | Choice architecture adds defaults, mapping, friction, feedback, transparency, and meaningful exit. |

: Five recurring cases and the new analytical layer added when each returns. {#tbl-recurring-case-map}

## Linked video cases

The book links to third-party videos rather than reproducing frames. Availability and rights remain with the linked providers. Some clips are optional lecture companions rather than examples retold in the core narrative. The table therefore names a primary conceptual owner and supplies a self-contained viewing question; if a link disappears, use the same question with a replacement scene or written vignette. Apply the viewing protocol in Appendix A: predict, observe, diagnose, qualify, and apply.

| Teaching moment | Primary owner | Link | Viewing question |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| Selective attention / awareness test | Ch. 3 | [Awareness example 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Wie4v2YCPQY) · [Awareness example 2](https://youtu.be/vBPG_OBgTWg) | What remained visible but failed to become evidence? |
